Firstly, high-purity metals (Mn > 99.9 wt.%, others > 99.99 wt.%) were selected as raw materials and ingots were melted in a vacuum arc melting furnace under an argon protection atmosphere. The ingots were re-melted at least 5 times, and continuous electromagnetic stirring was performed during the melting process to ensure uniformity of the alloys.
The melted ingots were then cast into a 7.8 × 12 × 58.5 mm3 mold.
The cast ingots were subjected to a solution treatment at 1200 ◦C for 4 h followed by water quenching.
Next, they were subjected to hot rolling at 900 ◦C with a cumulative reduction of 50%, followed by another solid solution treatment at 1200 ◦C for 2 h.
followed by another solid solution treatment at 1200 ◦C for 2 h. The resulting alloys were then subjected to multi-pass room temperature rolling with a total thickness reduction of 60%.
The resulting alloys were then subjected to multi-pass room temperature rolling with a total thickness reduction of 60%.

Subsequently, to obtain the partially recrystallized or the fully recrystallized microstructures with fine grains, short-term annealing was performed at 650, 750 and 850 ◦C for 3 min in a salt bath furnace followed by water quenching.
